source_prompt: Chris, 2026-09-24, /ai-jane d — 'Extract koros-arc-store-v1 from the two KIND app PRDs and reconcile both against it'. This answers the STRUCTURAL question both app-design sessions put to him on 2026-09-23: extract the shared scaffold into its own PRD, or merge the two app PRDs. He chose extract.
review_protocol: Written in Draft Mode on 2026-09-24 as an EXTRACTION, not a fresh design. Chris edits fullprompt.md in place with (CSH ...) markers; /ai-design --review koros-arc-store-v1 diffs the working tree against draft_commit, classifies every hunk, propagates through body, stories, testing decisions and taskplan, re-derives Gotchas, and recommits with a fresh baseline. The ready gate refuses advance while review_rounds is 0.

external_research.reason: Both parent PRDs ran a Maestro codex scan on h100, and the model-analysis scan (task-f379e8ac) addressed exactly this module's external question — whether RO-Crate or an MLflow-style index is the standard run-record envelope, and the failure modes of an append-only JSONL store. Its accepted recommendations (last-writer-wins on record_id; SQLite past a few thousand records) are in this design; RO-Crate was declined with a stated reason. A third scan over extracted text would restate them. This is a recorded decision with named prior work, not a skipped step.

build_order: koros-arc-store-v1 (p0a -> p0b -> p0c -> p0d, strictly sequential, all KBUtilLib) lands on main FIRST. Then the two apps are independent of each other, with two caveats: KBUtilLib is both this module's repo and the model-analysis app's repo, so that app cannot start while this builds (dev 1032 one-branch-per-repo); and both apps touch KBDLJobRunningPrototype, needing separate repo slots.

could_not_decide: Whether the KBDL object store is reachable from the kbhub pod. Bears on this module only through the obj://<object_id> artifact form: the vocabulary is fixed regardless, but whether such a ref resolves on a pod is unverified.

The CAC's own unfilled <fill:> seams in the id-normalization helper and the contract-version gate mechanics. p0c implements the documented behaviour; the rest will be settled by reading FJ's or genKnown's interop.py.

Whether 'official app in KOROS' means code contributed upstream into koros/king or our repo conforming to the CAC. Open for both consumers; does not bind this module under either reading, since the consume-only interlock means it never contributes upstream.

Whether re-runs should collapse to one row. record_id derives from kind + subject + significant_params, so an identical re-run replaces its predecessor and history is lost. The parent PRD flagged the counter-argument and did not resolve it; carried forward unresolved rather than quietly settled by extraction.

round_1.S11_note: THE BEST FIND, AND MY FIRST RESOLUTION OF IT WAS WRONG. The adversary spotted that 'hard-fail on major, warn on compatible minor' contradicts 'contract_version is an INTEGER'. I first wrote that there is no minor. Checking king/docs/CROSS_APP_COMMUNICATION.md showed the contradiction is UPSTREAM: the wire field is ruled an integer at :141/:173/:252, section F states semver gating at :290, and :294 marks the gate mechanics an explicit unfilled placeholder. Final resolution: implement integer comparison only -- equal proceeds, any difference hard-fails -- and implement no minor branch, because with an integer on the wire there is nothing to compare a minor against. Propagated into BOTH consumer apps, whose tasks required the warn-on-minor behaviour.
